newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bossi fined for insulting star magistrate.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bossi fined for insulting star magistrate.

text.p: An Italian court fined northern separatist leader Umberto Bossi and ordered him to pay substantial costs on Monday for insulting former star anti-graft magistrate Antonio Di Pietro.
Bossi, who did not attend the hearing, was fined 1.5 million lire ($1,000) for defamation and ordered to pay 60 million lire ($40,000) in damages and costs.

The case, which followed a complaint from Di Pietro, arose from a report in the newspaper Il Giornale in December 1995 which quoted Bossi as telling a rally of his Northern League party that Di Pietro was a "peasant".

The Italian word, "terrone", is considered a severe insult when aimed at southerners. Di Pietro, who spearheaded a judicial assault on political graft until he resigned as a magistrate at the end of 1994, is from the southern Molise region.

"We'll give Di Pietro a cardboard suitcase. It's a present that rhymes with peasant," Bossi, who has a reputation for blunt language, was quoted as saying. He was also quoted as saying that Di Pietro was working against the League.
Bossi and former League treasurer Alessandro Patelli were found guilty of receiving undeclared contributions for the party's 1992 election at a trial which ended in October 1995.
The trial, at which Di Pietro was prosecutor, involved 22 defendants including many of the leading figures in Italy's discredited old political class.
Di Pietro's lawyer Massimo Dinoia said Monday's ruling had refuted the notion that his client had pursued a political line in his investigations into corruption.
Il Giornale's editor Vittorio Feltri and the newspaper's reporter were cleared of wrongdoing at the hearing.
